tagline: Bitcoin, wild price swings, and Hong Kong's push to be a crypto hub.
why: Crypto went from a niche internet experiment to something Wall Street, governments and your colleagues talk about. Bitcoin is now held by ETFs and companies, stablecoins are being regulated, and Hong Kong has positioned itself as a licensed crypto hub. It's polarising: some see the future of money, others a casino. Knowing the basics lets you join in without being lost or preachy.

essentials.title: Bitcoin is digital gold
essentials.body: Created in 2009 by the pseudonymous Satoshi Nakamoto. Only 21 million will ever exist. Fans see it as a hedge against inflation and money printing.

essentials.title: Ethereum is a platform
essentials.body: Ethereum runs programs called smart contracts, which power stablecoins, DeFi and NFTs. Its coin is ether (ETH).

essentials.title: Stablecoins are crypto dollars
essentials.body: Coins like USDT (Tether) and USDC are pegged to the US dollar and used for trading and payments. They're now being regulated in the US and Hong Kong.

essentials.title: Prices are extremely volatile
essentials.body: Bitcoin has crashed more than 70% several times and recovered to new highs. Altcoins swing even more.

essentials.title: The cycle and the halving
essentials.body: Every four years Bitcoin's new supply is halved. Many believe prices move in four-year boom-and-bust cycles around it.

essentials.title: Wall Street adoption
essentials.body: US spot Bitcoin ETFs launched in January 2024 and drew huge inflows. Companies like Strategy hold Bitcoin on their balance sheets.

essentials.title: Self-custody vs exchanges
essentials.body: You can hold coins on an exchange or in your own wallet. 'Not your keys, not your coins' warns that exchanges can fail, as FTX did.

timeline.event: The Bitcoin white paper is published.
Someone buys two pizzas for 10,000 BTC: 'Bitcoin Pizza Day'.
Mt. Gox, the biggest exchange, collapses.
First big boom: Bitcoin nears $20,000; ICO mania.
Bitcoin hits about $69,000; NFT mania; El Salvador makes it legal tender.
Crypto winter: Terra/Luna and FTX collapse.
US spot Bitcoin ETFs approved; Hong Kong launches spot Bitcoin and Ether ETFs; Bitcoin passes $100,000.
US passes the GENIUS Act for stablecoins; Hong Kong's stablecoin law takes effect; Bitcoin hits a record above $120,000 in October, then falls sharply.

now.headline: Bitcoin slides toward US$62k
now.detail: Bitcoin hit a three-month low of about US$62,080 on 15 November, down roughly 15% in a week, before bouncing to around US$65,000.

now.headline: ETF money is leaving
now.detail: US spot Bitcoin ETFs saw about US$1.91 billion of outflows over seven straight sessions from 5 to 13 November, per Farside Investors.

now.headline: A liquidation wave
now.detail: About US$1.96 billion of leveraged crypto bets were wiped out in 24 hours, around US$750 million of them in Bitcoin and mostly longs.

now.headline: Altcoins hit harder
now.detail: Ether is down to about US$1,790, Solana about US$70, and XRP has slipped below US$1.

now.headline: Rate-hike fears
now.detail: Hot October inflation (CPI +0.4% on the month), a 10-year Treasury yield above 5% and a likely Fed hike in December are hitting crypto hardest.

now.headline: Levels to watch
now.detail: Glassnode flags a cluster of liquidations around US$60,000-62,000; below that, June's low of about US$58,559 is the floor traders talk about.

local.headline: Licensed hub
local.detail: Hong Kong's SFC licenses crypto exchanges, and only licensed platforms can serve retail investors.

local.headline: Stablecoin ordinance
local.detail: Since August 2025, issuing a stablecoin in Hong Kong needs an HKMA licence. Big local firms applied.

local.headline: The JPEX scandal
local.detail: In 2023 an unlicensed exchange, JPEX, collapsed with big losses for local investors, leading to arrests.

local.headline: Crypto ETFs
local.detail: Hong Kong has spot Bitcoin and Ether ETFs you can buy through a normal brokerage.

debates.question: Is Bitcoin real money or speculation?
debates.sides: Fans call it digital gold; critics say it has no intrinsic value.

debates.question: Should crypto be regulated?
debates.sides: Regulation brings safety and legitimacy, but purists say it undermines the point.

debates.question: Will stablecoins replace banks?
debates.sides: They could make payments faster and cheaper, but raise stability concerns.

debates.question: Is it too late to buy?
debates.sides: Believers say it's early; sceptics say late buyers fund early holders.
